checks for
photo search
slides.accentLine: Search Console now shows traffic from Lens and Circle to Search.

slides.title: Open the new
slides.body: Since Sept 24, 2026, Search Console counts searches made with Lens, Circle to Search and image uploads.
slides.action: Performance → Search type → Web: multimodal. Then open the Pages tab.
slides.example: A shoe page found when someone uses Lens on a shoe they like.

slides.title: Check the
slides.body: The same filter works in the Generative AI performance report for Google Search.
slides.action: Open the Generative AI report and set the search type to Web: multimodal.
slides.example: Compare text-based and multimodal impressions for one product page.

slides.title: Write useful
slides.body: Google calls alt text the most important image metadata and uses it with computer vision.
slides.action: Describe what is in the photo in a few specific words. No keyword lists.
slides.example: “image1” becomes “black leather ankle boot, side view”.

slides.title: Use real
slides.body: Google finds images in the src of an img element. It says it doesn't index CSS images.
slides.action: Check that key product photos are img tags, not only CSS backgrounds.
slides.example: A hero photo set as a CSS background-image on a category page.

slides.title: Name files,
slides.body: Google reads captions and nearby text. Filenames give it very light clues.
slides.action: Rename key photos descriptively and place them near relevant text.
slides.example: IMG00023.JPG becomes black-ankle-boot.jpg, next to the size guide.

slides.title: Five checks,
slides.seed: An AI can draft alt text from your product names.
